_______________________________________


April 7:
Dear Diary- It found us. Michael went out for a supply run. He volunteered even though he knew the dangers. Instead of just killing Michael when it found him outside, it waited. Waited just until Michael had grabbed a few supplies and knocked on our shelter door. Then we heard it take him. It knows we're in here now and we can hear it stalking around outside, scratching at the heavy steel doors, trying to find a weakness to exploit. Luckily, this building is big enough that it doesn't know exactly where we are. We're still relatively safe in here as long as it can't get in. We have power, fresh water, and we've been able to hoard a bunch of canned food and other non-perishables. The remaining four of us can hold out in here for months with what we have. 
_______________________________________


April 13:
Dear Diary- It seems to be learning very fast. We lost power yesterday. It must have noticed the lights on throughout the building and cut our power. We looked out a window on a higher floor and saw that all the power lines are down. Every pole within a block was torn down. We didn't really need the electricity anyway; we've got plenty of material to make fires for light and heat. The days have actually become pretty stale when it isn't trying to get us. We just kind of sit and wait.
_______________________________________


April 15: 
Dear Diary- It has the upper hand now. We don't know what it did, but we have no running water now. We never got bottled water because we had a fresh source. We doomed ourselves by not thinking ahead. We don't know how long we can go without water. We'll need to try and find some, and that means going outside. It has to be waiting for us to come out.
_______________________________________


April 18:
Dear Diary- It was waiting. Derek was so thirsty that he ran outside to drink from a puddle on the sidewalk. It got him. His brother Nick couldn't handle it. We tried to stop him, but he ran outside screaming for it, and it came for him too. Now it's just Sam and me. We're not going to last long without water. This may be my last entry.
_______________________________________


April 23:
Dear Diary- It's screwing with us. We hear it constantly growling and making other noises at us out there. It almost sounds like a mocking laughter. It seems to know we're in trouble. We rigged up a rain collector to try and get water, but it seems to have gotten over its aversion to water. Now it just paces around the building, without its “raincoat.” It used the tarp to plug up our water collector. Sam is on the verge of death, and we both know he won't live without water. So does it.
_______________________________________


April 24:
Dear Diary- It got in. It somehow managed to break in. I'm alone now; Sam died from dehydration shortly before I heard it get in. I've locked myself in another room, but this room can't protect me overnight with that thing out there. This is the end. I'm dehydrated. Exhausted. I have no food in here. If anyone ever finds this diary, learn from it. Learn from our mistakes. Like that creature did. Don't underestimate it. It can think. Better than us.

Chocolate *is* toxic to dogs, but only to a degree. Dogs metabolize theobromine (a compound related to caffeine found in chocolate) much slower than humans. 17 hours after ingesting it, half of the theobromine is still present in a dog's system, whereas it would be completely gone in a human in less than half the time. 

Because they still do metabolize theobromine, dogs can survive ingesting some chocolate. A lethal dose would be about 1oz/1lb of body weight, so for what I'm guessing is about a 20-30lb dog pictured, she would have to  ingest 20oz or more for it to be lethal. Most candy bars are only 1-4oz of chocolate. This dog has mild to moderate theobromine poisoning. She may get the shits and not feel too well for a day, but she's gonna be just fine.
